rc-leader.title: When a leader can tell the client a write succeeded
rc-leader.description: A write reaches the leader, commits there, is confirmed by the first follower, and is then confirmed by all followers; asynchronous, semi-synchronous, and synchronous replication acknowledge at successive points.
rc-leader.note: Each later point risks fewer lost writes and makes commits slower.

rc-lag.title: Read-your-writes using a log position
rc-lag.description: A write commits at a log position, the server remembers that position for the user, and a later read on a lagging follower waits or goes to the leader until the follower has reached it.
rc-lag.note: The position answers the question exactly; a time window only guesses at lag.

rc-order.title: Two read anomalies and the fix for each
rc-order.description: Reads can go backward when requests hit followers with different lag, which pinning fixes, and an effect can appear before its cause when shards lag differently, which one shared log fixes.
rc-order.note: Pinning stops reads going backward; one shared log keeps cause before effect.

items.title: Pin the reader
items.detail: hash user ID to one follower

items.title: Share one log
items.detail: key both events by order ID

rc-failover.title: Failing over, from detection to fencing
rc-failover.description: The cluster detects a dead leader, promotes the most caught-up follower under a new term, rejects writes carrying the old term, and redirects clients to the new leader.
rc-failover.note: Fencing stops new damage; writes that never left the old leader are still lost.

items.title: Redirect clients
items.detail: writes go to the new leader

rc-multi.title: Four ways to handle a multi-leader write conflict
rc-multi.description: Conflicts can be avoided with a home region, settled by last-write-wins, merged automatically with CRDTs, or kept as versions for the application or user to resolve.
rc-multi.note: A rule like sell this room once needs a single owner, not resolution afterward.

rc-leaderless.title: Matching four workloads to a replication model
rc-leaderless.description: Seat reservations fit a single leader, an offline notes app and regional profiles fit multiple leaders, and sensor readings fit a leaderless store.
rc-leaderless.note: Ask what should happen when two writes touch the same item at once.
